address: 349-351 Nguyễn Trãi, Ward 7, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: Hoa (Chinese-Vietnamese) noodle house going since the 1970s; the signature mì vịt tiềm pairs a lightly-fried, herb-braised duck leg with springy egg noodles in a thuốc-bắc broth, plus crisp fried wontons. A Chợ Lớn benchmark for the dish.
dish: mì vịt tiềm (herbal braised-duck egg-noodle soup)

n: Hủ Tiếu Sa Tế Tô Ký
address: Gia Phú, Ward 1, District 6, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: Nearly-80-year-old Teochew family shop (founded by Tô Cẩm, now third generation) famous for hủ tiếu sa tế nai — a fiery, nutty satay broth built from 20-30 spices, peanuts and sesame poured over noodles with sliced venison. The reference for the dish in Chợ Lớn.
dish: hủ tiếu sa tế nai (Teochew satay venison noodle soup)

address: 18 Cao Đạt, Ward 1, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A long-standing three-floor Chợ Lớn dim sum institution singled out by Michelin-recognised chef DoBee Lam as a favourite old-school điểm tâm hall — steamer carts of har gow, siu mai, cheung fun and Cantonese classics from morning.

n: Sủi Cảo Hà Tôn Quyền (Thiên Thiên)
address: Hà Tôn Quyền, Ward 4, District 11, Cholon, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: The heart of Saigon's nicknamed 'phố sủi cảo' — a cluster of Hoa family dumpling shops (Thiên Thiên among the best-known) that have run for 30+ years each. Plump shrimp-and-pork sủi cảo steamed, fried, or in clear soup with handmade noodles.

address: Chợ Phùng Hưng, Phùng Hưng, Ward 14, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A 70-year-old Hoa cà phê vợt (cloth-'sock'-filter coffee) stall tucked in Phùng Hưng market, roasting its own beans on site over wood with a touch of butter and salt. A living Cantonese coffee-culture relic of Chợ Lớn.

address: Trần Hưng Đạo B, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: An ~80-year-old Cantonese dessert cart (opened 1938 by a Guangdong immigrant), nicknamed Chè Cột Điện and Chè Ma for its lamppost spot and late hours. Warm and iced Chinese sweet soups — almond, black-sesame, lotus and herbal chè — done the old way.

address: Châu Văn Liêm, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A Chợ Lớn dumpling stalwart on Châu Văn Liêm known for chive-packed sủi cảo — soft-yet-chewy dumplings loaded with garlic-chive; also plates a Chinese-style phá lấu. A neighbourhood authority on the craft.

address: 823 Nguyễn Trãi, Ward 14, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A 60-year, three-generation Teochew phá lấu cart on Nguyễn Trãi: pork ears, tongue, tripe, chicken feet and tofu braised in a five-spice, star-anise and cinnamon master stock, with a sweet Teochew dipping sauce. Also famed for its bánh mì phá lấu.

address: 83 An Điềm, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A half-century-old Hoa dessert shop beloved by Chợ Lớn's Chinese community for nearly 30 gently-sweet Cantonese chè — almond tofu (đậu hũ hạnh nhân), steamed-egg custard, black sesame and egg tea. Opens late afternoon.
dish: đậu hũ hạnh nhân (almond tofu chè) and Cantonese sweet soups

address: Chợ Phùng Hưng, Phùng Hưng, Ward 14, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A rare taste of Chợ Lớn's Hakka (Hẹ) heritage: khổ qua cà ớt — bitter melon, chili and tomato stuffed with fish paste in a clear soup. A near-vanished home-style dish kept alive by a Phùng Hưng-market family stall.
dish: khổ qua cà ớt (fish-paste-stuffed bitter melon & chili soup)

address: District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: An unassuming Chợ Lớn spot serving top-notch Taiwanese home-style comfort cooking — braises, rice bowls and hot soups — a Chinese-diaspora counterpoint to the Cantonese/Teochew canon around it.
